title: Using AI in Student Creative Art Translations and STEM Workshop
summary: RHGE reports that girls in Nigerian community schools created AI-assisted art and advocacy projects. The activities expand creative practice; learning effects are not quantified.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: RHGE reports that girls in Nigerian community schools created AI-assisted art and advocacy projects in workshops. The activities expand creative practice, while learning effects remain unquantified.
purpose: Expand girls' creative and STEM participation through AI-assisted activities.
system: RHGE generative-AI creative-art and STEM workshops
location: Kubwa, Dei Dei, Dutse, and Byazhin, Abuja FCT, Nigeria

ratings.reason: RHGE reports that girls created AI-assisted digital artworks, narratives, and advocacy projects. Long-term learning and employment effects are unknown.
RHGE reports expanding its workshops with AI-assisted simulations and creative production. Financial returns are unmeasured.

ai_role.statement: Generative AI helps students transform artwork into digital forms, produce narratives, and visualize STEM concepts. Teachers, workshops, and supporting organizations remain central to the activities.

evidence.citation: Project account in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. Outcomes are reported by the project team. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use case -9: Using AI in Student Creative Art Translations and STEM Workshop

produced_by: Conditions that could produce the benefit are unspecified.
must_hold: Facilitated school workshops and access to creative AI tools
Teacher and community support for student projects

headline: Girls use generative AI in creative and STEM workshops
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
